notes: Account: Holloway Inference (global fintech data platform). Heavy compliance needs; high sensitivity PII in logs.
Primary ask: enterprise Dedicated cluster with hard throughput guarantees for realtime chat and large-scale reranking workloads.
AE/Jordan: engaged since Nov '25; POC completed Feb '26. POC summary sent and discussed 2026-02-18 (see Fireflies).
POC results: 8xA100 equiv sustained throughput for embeddings pipeline; chat latencies within target for single-tenant run but variance under multi-tenant test.
They want a binding min-tokens/sec commitment (sustained) with clear failure/credit terms — major negotiation point.
Quote from CTO on call: 'We need a floor not a best-effort; spikes are fine but baseline is business-critical.'
Budget band: $500k–$1M ARR; procurement timeline pushed to Apr 2026 contingent on SLA language and residency confirmation.
Security: require KMS integration, SOC2 attestation, audit logs to be retained for 7 years, and ability to restrict model telemetry outside their VPC.
Deployment preference: VPC-hosted Dedicated with an option for an on-prem appliance for air-gapped staging (later phase).

Internal champion: Head of ML Ops (Rebecca Holloway) — engaged and pushing for deterministic throughput for latency-sensitive features.
Current ask from procurement: provide explicit min_tokens/sec metric, concurrency caps and clear burst policy (how many tokens and for how long).
They ran a stress test during POC: sustained 48k tokens/sec @ p95 latency ~110ms on a 10 GPU configuration; want 45k/min guarantee with 2x burst for 15 minutes.
AE notes: propose Dedicated plan: 12 reserved GPUs + 2 pre-warmed hot spares to meet burst window; include quantified overage pricing and credits scheme.
SE notes (Ava): recommend KV cache per-customer, sticky routing to avoid cold-start penalties; advise pinned model variant to reduce kernel variance.
Finance ask: define clear metric mapping used in billing and SLA (tokens billed vs tokens guaranteed; measurement windows; smoothing).
Risk items: model upgrades causing latency regressions — discuss rollback and canary policy in rollout section of SLA.
Next internal deliverable: draft SLA addendum with min_tokens/sec, p99 latency targets, concurrency caps, burst policy, and credit calculation by 2026-03-10.

throughput_targets: min_tokens_per_sec: 45,000 (sustained across reserved capacity, measured as 1-hour rolling average)
p95_latency: <90ms for streaming first-byte on chat (local region); p99_latency: <150ms end-to-end
concurrency_cap: baseline 600 concurrent sessions (avg request 120 tokens), with headroom planning to 900 for bursts
burst_policy: allowed 2x sustained throughput for up to 15 minutes; burst consumption met from pre-warmed pool; over-burst billed at defined overage rates
pre-warm_policy: 2 hot spare GPUs to cover short-term capacity spikes; warm-up time target <30s for sticky sessions
measurement_window: SLA windows are 1h rolling for throughput, 24h for credits calculation; monitoring hooks required for token counts and per-route attribution
sla_preferences: Credits model: hourly credit for shortfalls >1% of guaranteed tokens/sec over measurement window
Failure modes: automatic fallback to compatible hosted model with rate-limited throughput if Dedicated capacity degraded
Penalty cap: credits capped at monthly committed spend; negotiation point on how fast Redwood can add capacity in region
Operational expectations: 24x7 priority support, 1-hour response for Sev1, quarterly business reviews
